The first meeting of the joint defense industry committee took place in Brazil on Monday (local time), led by officials of Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) and Brazil's defense ministry, DAPA said in a release. Korea views Brazil as a strategic partner in its push to diversify arms exports to the Central and South American regions. Seoul plans to purchase three Brazilian-made Embraer C-390 Millennium tactical airlifters for its Air Force to boost its troop transport and aerial refueling capabilities under the second phase of its large transport aircraft acquisition program. Han made the remark at the start of a meeting of the government's task force on ensuring exam fairness, instructing ministries in charge of respective exams to look into whether cheating using artificial intelligence (AI) and other high-tech means had occurred in past exams. "We should closely examine problems raised in the press, reports of suspected cheating and unusual score patterns, and take all possible measures, including stripping licenses and criminal punishment, if cheating is actually confirmed," Han said. Exam cheating has been one of the hottest topics in Korea in recent weeks, following the confession earlier this month by the top scorer of this year's certified tax accountant exam that he cheated with the help of AI and that he also used the same method on a certified public accountant exam. items.summary: Seoul is inviting residents to turn down their home heating and head to nearby libraries this winter, pairing an energy-saving campaign with hundreds of reading and cultural programs across the city. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Tuesday that 214 libraries, including Seoul Metropolitan Library, will participate in its Off & Library campaign from Dec. 1 through Feb. 28, 2027. The initiative, titled Libraries Are Hot, encourages residents to switch off their heating temporarily and spend time reading or enjoying cultural activities in warm public spaces, reducing household energy consumption during the coldest months. Now in its fourth year, Seoul Metropolitan Library's seasonal climate campaign has featured separate summer and winter editions, promoting libraries as places to escape extreme temperatures while encouraging everyday energy conservation. items.title: Lawmaker referred to prosecutors over alleged corruption, bribery

items.summary: Police on Tuesday referred independent lawmaker Kim Byung-kee to prosecutors over various corruption allegations, such as taking bribes. Kim, formerly of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), faces allegations of accepting tens of millions of won in exchange for legislative favors for cryptocurrency exchange Bithumb and a transport system company. He is also suspected of overlooking allegations that a former DPK lawmaker took 100 million won ($74,400) in bribes ahead of the 2022 local elections, and accepting a hotel voucher from Korean Air, among other allegations. The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's public crimes unit sent the cases to the prosecution, recommending multiple charges, including acceptance of bribes and obstruction of business. Kim quit the DPK in January after stepping down as the party's floor leader the previous month over the mounting allegations.

items.title: Grace period to regularize status of GCC-registered vehicles expires
items.title_zh: 规范海合会注册车辆状态的宽限期已到期
items.summary: RIYADH — The 90-day grace period for vehicles registered in Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and present in the Kingdom to regularize their status expired on Monday. The grace period was granted by the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority in cooperation with the Ministry of Interior, represented by the General Directorate of Traffic. Running from August 26 to November 23, the grace period allowed vehicle owners to regularize their status either by exporting their vehicles from the Kingdom or completing the registration procedures and obtaining Saudi license plates. Under the regulations, GCC vehicles owned by Saudi citizens or non-GCC residents, as well as vehicles driven by individuals authorized to do so, may remain in the Kingdom for no more than 90 days, whether consecutive or non-consecutive, within any 365-day period. The period is calculated from the date the vehicle enters the Kingdom through a customs port. The authority clarified that vehicle owners can regularize their status either by exporting their vehicles from the Kingdom or registering them and obtaining Saudi license plates. The procedures can be completed by authorizing a customs broker to submit the customs declaration through the nearest port of entry, fulfil the relevant requirements, and pay the applicable fees and taxes, without having to return to the original port of entry. The authority also introduced a service through the Absher platform, in coordination with the General Directorate of Traffic, allowing vehicle owners to request an extension of their vehicles' stay for up to 30 additional days, provided the request is submitted before the expiry of the legally permitted period.

items.title: Health ministry takes legal action against sick leave violators
items.title_zh: 卫生部对违反病假规定的行为采取法律行动
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Health has taken legal action against violators of its sick leave regulations. As part of its inspection campaign, the ministry officials carried out 1,817 visits across regions of Saudi Arabia. Using an advanced monitoring methodology, the campaign identified 116,131 sick leave certificates requiring verification of their lawful issuance. The monitoring process revealed several patterns that helped identify potential violations, most notably the issuance of 70,753 sick leave certificates by a single healthcare facility and 9,584 by a single healthcare practitioner. It also detected 259 certificates issued by one practitioner in a single day and 46,279 certificates linked to noncompliant healthcare facilities. Inspection teams subsequently initiated on-site verification procedures and took the necessary measures.The campaign resulted in legal action against violators, including individuals who sought to obtain an unauthorized number of sick leave certificates or certificates from unlicensed sources, as well as entities that failed to comply with regulations. Measures included suspending relevant authorizations and referring cases to the competent authorities.The campaign was part of the ministry’s efforts to strengthen compliance with regulations, ensure the reliability of sick leave certificates, and protect beneficiaries' rights. The ministry reaffirmed its commitment to protecting beneficiaries' rights and emphasized the importance of professionalism among healthcare practitioners and strict adherence to applicable instructions, regulations, and controls.

items.title: KFSH honors 41 researchers named among world’s top 2% scientists by Stanford
items.title_zh: 斯坦福大学将41名研究人员列入全球前2%科学家名单，KFSH对此表示祝贺
items.summary: RIYADH — King Faisal Specialist Hospital & Research Centre (KFSH) honored on Monday 41 of its scientists and researchers after they were named among the world’s top 2 percent most-cited scientists in Stanford University’s annual ranking. The number represents an increase of six researchers compared with last year and marks the seventh consecutive year that KFSH researchers have appeared on the prestigious list, reflecting the hospital’s growing contribution to international scientific research. Stanford’s ranking evaluates researchers using a range of citation-based indicators that measure the impact of their scientific work, both throughout their careers and within a single year. These indicators provide insights into the influence of researchers’ publications and their contributions to advancing scientific knowledge across various disciplines. The recognition comes as KFSH continues to strengthen its position in international research rankings. The hospital ranked first among healthcare institutions in Saudi Arabia in the 2025 Nature Index, which tracks scientific research published in 145 leading journals across the natural and health sciences. The journals included in the index are selected by an independent panel of researchers and experts based on their scientific reputation and impact. KFSH also ranked first in the Middle East and Africa and 12th globally among the world’s top 250 academic medical centers for 2026. In addition, Brand Finance named KFSH the most valuable healthcare brand in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East for 2026. The hospital was also included in Newsweek’s World’s Best Hospitals 2026 ranking, as well as its World’s Best Smart Hospitals 2027 and World’s Best Specialized Hospitals 2027 rankings.

items.title: Health ministry dismisses Wasfati service cancellation rumors
items.title_zh: 卫生部驳斥Wasfati服务取消的传言
items.summary: RIYADH — The Saudi Ministry of Health has denied reports claiming the cancellation of the “Wasfati” (my prescription) service, affirming that the service remains operational and continues to undergo development and expansion. The ministry stressed that reports circulating about the cancellation of the service are inaccurate. The ministry emphasized its commitment to further developing and expanding it to enhance healthcare quality and improve the user experience.In a statement on his X account, Ministry of Health spokesperson Abdulaziz Abdulbaqi said that “Wasfati” is one of the specialized services under the Health Sector Transformation Program. He noted that the service helps facilitate access to medications and enhance the efficiency of healthcare services.It is noteworthy that Wasfati is an electronic prescription service supervised by the Ministry of Health and managed by National Unified Procurement Company (NUPCO) that connects hospitals and primary health care centers with accredited community pharmacies so eligible patients can receive prescribed medications for free.

items.title: Saudi Crown Prince calls Emir of Kuwait to inquire about his health
items.title_zh: 沙特王储致电科威特埃米尔，询问其健康状况
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman held on Monday a phone call with Emir of Kuwait Sheikh Meshal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah. During the call, the Crown Prince conveyed the greetings of Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman to the Emir and his wishes for continued good health. The Crown Prince also inquired about the Emir's health, wishing him continued health and well-being. The Emir of Kuwait expressed his gratitude to King Salman and the Crown Prince for their kind fraternal sentiments.

items.title: Industry ministry issues nearly 56,000 Certificates of Origin in October
items.title_zh: 工业和信息化部10月份签发近5.6万份原产地证书
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources issued 55,965 Certificates of Origin in October 2026. This was part of its efforts to support and streamline the service for exporters across the industrial, commercial, and individual sectors.The ministry said in a statement that a Certificate of Origin is a document certifying that exported products are of national origin or have acquired that status.The service targets industrial establishments, commercial companies and institutions, as well as individuals, including farmers, fishermen, people engaged in individual activities, local artisans, and others. The ministry explained that the certificate is available in four formats: a Certificate of Origin for national products destined for Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries; a Certificate of Origin for national products destined for Arab countries; a Preferential Certificate of Origin, which is the unified form adopted by the GCC for exports to countries and economic blocs with which free trade agreements have been concluded; and a bilingual (Arabic and English) Certificate of Origin for countries that do not grant preferential treatment (the general form).Beneficiaries can apply for a Certificate of Origin through the ministry's website.

items.title: Absher carries out over 45 million electronic transactions in October
items.title_zh: Absher在10月份完成了超过4500万笔电子交易
items.summary: RIYADH — The Ministry of Interior’s electronic platform Absher has processed a total of 45,168,522 electronic transactions for beneficiaries during October.Through the Absher Individuals platform, total transactions reached 42,607,799, and these include 33,989,242 document viewings through the digital document wallet, which is accessible to citizens, residents, and visitors via the Absher application. Meanwhile, the Absher Businesses platform recorded 2,560,723 transactions.The General Directorate of Public Security processed 3,539,011 transactions, including 3,400,356 by the General Directorate of Traffic, 2,328,379 by the General Directorate of Passports, and 450,714 by the Ministry of Interior’s Civil Status Agency. Through the Absher Individuals platform, 108,073 reports were issued using the Absher Reports service, while 2,100 general inquiries related to fingerprinting were processed.It is noteworthy that the unified digital IDs issued by the Ministry of Interior through the Absher platform enable citizens, residents, and visitors to access services provided by the ministry’s various sectors easily and securely through its electronic platforms: Absher Individuals, Absher Businesses, and Absher Government. They also facilitate access to services offered by government and private entities through the National Unified Access Portal Nafath.

items.title: Saudi, Norwegian foreign ministers discuss regional situation in phone call
items.title_zh: 沙特与挪威外长通过电话讨论地区局势
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Minister of Foreign Affairs Prince Faisal bin Farhan held a phone call with Norwegian Minister of Foreign Affairs Espen Barth Eide. During the call, the ministers reviewed bilateral relations between the two countries and opportunities to strengthen them. They also discussed the latest regional developments and ongoing efforts to address them.

items.title: Indonesia signs Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh
items.title_zh: 印度尼西亚签署2030年利雅得世博会参展合同
items.summary: JAKARTA — Indonesia has signed its Participation Contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh, marking an important step as it progresses its participation in the World Expo. The Participation Contract was signed in Indonesia by Chief Executive Officer of Expo 2030 Riyadh Talal Al-Marri and Indonesia's Minister for National Development Planning/Head of Bappenas Rachmat Pambudy. Indonesia’s signing adds to an expanding international community formalizing its participation in Expo 2030 Riyadh. More than 185 Official Participants have already confirmed their participation, demonstrating the truly global character of a World Expo and the breadth of experiences and perspectives that will come together in Riyadh in 2030.Pambudy said: “The early signing of our participation contract for Expo 2030 Riyadh reflects our readiness to lead through partnership and strengthen ties between Indonesia and Saudi Arabia. Building on the momentum of Expo 2025 Osaka, which generated over $28 billion in investment commitments for Indonesia, we view Riyadh as a vital platform for economic diplomacy where Golden Indonesia 2045 and Saudi Vision 2030 converge to turn shared foresight into lasting, concrete development outcomes.” Looking ahead, Indonesia will bring its story to life in the Planet District at Expo 2030 Riyadh, showcasing the richness of its heritage, the creativity of its people and its ambitions for the future through a unique pavilion that celebrates its identity while sharing its vision with the world. Pambudy added: “Our vision for Expo 2030 Riyadh goes far beyond a six-month exhibition. We want the Indonesia Pavilion to serve as a lasting meeting point where governments, businesses, and investors turn ideas into concrete development outcomes. Guided by our theme, ‘Nature Unfolding: Explore, Wisdom, Nurture,’ and the Indonesian philosophy that nature is our greatest teacher, we are bringing a unified national commitment to Riyadh, demonstrating how wisdom and collective action can shape a sustainable, inclusive, and prosperous future for generations to come.” On this occasion, Al-Marri said: “Indonesia is a powerful example of what becomes possible when different cultures and communities come together while retaining what makes them distinct. That same possibility lies at the heart of a World Expo – bringing countries and cultures together around a shared purpose, to learn from one another and explore what we can achieve together. We are delighted that Indonesia will be part of Expo 2030 Riyadh and look forward to seeing its contribution to the World Expo take shape.” Expo 2030 Riyadh is advancing at pace across all elements of delivery. Alongside continued progress on international participation, delivery is accelerating across the six-million-square-metre site, with construction activity scaling up, major infrastructure works advancing and key vertical assets taking shape. Held under the theme “Foresight for Tomorrow,” Expo 2030 Riyadh will provide a platform for nations to showcase their achievements and ambitions, explore solutions to shared challenges and inspire new possibilities for the future. Across five thematic areas, Technology, Planet, Humanity, Culture and Collaboration, Expo 2030 Riyadh will invite participants and visitors to engage with the ideas and perspectives shaping the decades ahead.

items.title: Saudi Arabia tightens childcare regulations with stricter safety standards, licensing rules
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯收紧托育机构监管，出台更严格的安全标准和许可规则
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi Arabia's updated regulations for private childcare centers introduce stricter safety standards, three-day licensing and penalties of up to license revocation for violations. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development announced the amendments on Monday to improve service quality and child protection. Under the updated regulations, licenses must be issued within three working days once all requirements are met. The amendments also revise standards for facilities, equipment, capacity, staffing and safety. The regulations establish updated child-to-caregiver ratios based on age groups, alongside qualification and experience requirements for staff. Childcare centers must implement policies covering child protection, emergency procedures, complaints, parental communication, nutrition, employee development and payment and refund arrangements. Centers are also required to provide parents with daily reports on their children and monthly assessments of acquired skills. The amendments introduce additional requirements for accommodating children with disabilities, including accessible facilities, assistive equipment and qualified personnel. Updated oversight measures establish procedures for addressing violations and deadlines for corrective action, with penalties ranging from warnings and operational suspensions to license revocation. The ministry said the changes aim to strengthen regulatory compliance, improve childcare services and provide safer environments that support children's development.
